purpose: Post-consolidation baseline for the German villa-buying query cluster (8 near-identical buy-intent queries, ~2,713 combined impressions, all previously stuck at position 12.8-24.6). Captured the same day four cannibalizing pages were merged into /de/luxusvillen-in-zypern. Compare against a fresh pull of the SAME 8 queries in ~1 month to see whether consolidation moved the flagship into the top 10, and whether the two remaining live competitors' traffic migrates to the flagship or simply disappears.
caveat: GSC's own reporting lags several days and keeps revising for roughly a month after each date (see the SearchMetric ingest investigation, 2026-08-31) -- the numbers below reflect data from BEFORE today's changes went live; nothing here yet shows any effect of the consolidation. Position/impression movement measured a month from now could be caused by the consolidation, by ordinary rank drift (this cluster showed real day-to-day and week-to-week drift throughout the investigation, independent of any site change), or by Google still processing the removal of four now-301'd competing URLs from its index, a process GSC's own documentation says can take weeks. Do not attribute 100% of any observed movement to the consolidation without checking whether comparable, untouched pages moved similarly over the same period as a control -- same discipline as the off-plan baseline (docs/paphos-offplan-baseline-2026-08-27.json).
ingestCaveat: Separately from the GSC-side lag above: these figures come from SearchMetric BEFORE its one-time 90-day backfill has run (held pending a clean first cron cycle under the widened 30-day re-fetch window -- see the SearchMetric ingest fix, 2026-08-31/09-01). Every historical row was captured once, 2 days after its date, under the old 3-day window, and never revisited -- so ABSOLUTE impressions/clicks below are undercounted relative to what GSC itself will eventually report for the same dates. Read this file for RELATIVE movement only (does a page's position improve, does impression share shift from one page to another) -- do not treat the raw impression numbers as true totals, and do not compare them directly against a fresh GSC export pulled outside SearchMetric.

window.note: queries[] and pageLevelTotalsAllTime below are all-time SearchMetric sums for each canonicalized page (query-level rows for the 8-query breakdown, page-level query:null rows for the totals) -- not a fixed rolling window. Freshest SearchMetric data as of capture: 2026-08-31 (normal ~1-day lag after the DAILY_WINDOW_DAYS widening, not stale).

queryMethodology: Query-level SearchMetric rows for the 8 cluster queries, canonicalized via urlCanonical.ts's canonicalize() to pool genuine bare/prefixed duplicates of the SAME live page (e.g. en::/luxusvillen-in-zypern with de::/de/luxusvillen-in-zypern) -- but NOT folded together with stale index carryover from pages that have since 301-redirected here (grosse-villen-zypern, haeuser-auf-zypern, etc.), since blending a live page's position with an already-redirected page's stale, un-refreshed position drags the number down without meaning anything (confirmed directly during the investigation this baseline follows). Same methodology as Part A of the investigation this baseline documents.
